title: Insert Interval
description:
You receive a list of pair-shaped closed intervals [start, end] and one more closed interval newInterval. The existing list is already sorted by increasing start and its intervals are strictly separated. Insert the new interval and unite every interval that intersects it. Return a new list covering exactly the same points as all original intervals plus the inserted one.

Closed intervals that share an endpoint intersect, so [1,2] and [2,4] become [1,4]. Emit intervals completely before the new range, expand the range while subsequent intervals touch it, then emit everything after it. Because starts are ordered, once an interval is strictly beyond the expanded end, none of the later intervals can reach back to join it.

The returned intervals must be sorted by start ascending, breaking equal starts by end ascending; the merged ranges are maximal and have no shared endpoints. Do not alter the caller’s input arrays. If intervals is empty, return a one-element list containing newInterval.

Example 1:

Input: intervals = [[1,3],[6,9]], newInterval = [2,5]
Output: [[1,5],[6,9]]

Example 2:

Input: intervals = [[1,2],[5,6],[8,10]], newInterval = [2,8]
Output: [[1,10]]

Example 3:

Input: intervals = [], newInterval = [4,7]
Output: [[4,7]]

Constraints:

  • 0 <= intervals.length <= 100,000
  • -1,000,000 <= start <= end <= 1,000,000
  • Existing intervals have strictly separated endpoints: intervals[i][1] < intervals[i+1][0].

exampleTestCases.explanation: The new range intersects the first range.
Endpoint contact merges all three old ranges.
